## `virtualization.partition.cpu.count`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `virtualization.partition.cpu.count` | UpDownCounter | `{vcpu}` | The number of virtual processors of the specified type currently allocated to the firmware partition. [1] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.partition` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[1]:** Reports the current virtual processor allocation for the partition. In IBM Z PR/SM (classic mode) this maps to the processor-count-* fields on the logical-partition or partition object in the HMC Web Services API. Analogous to `mainframe.partition.cpu.virtual.count` in the mainframe namespace.

**Attributes:**

| Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`virtualization.partition.id`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-partition-id) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | Unique identifier for the hardware or firmware partition. [1] | `0abc1234-5678-90ab-cdef-1234567890ab`; `partition-3` |
| [`virtualization.partition.cpu.type`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-partition-cpu-type) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The category of processor type allocated to the firmware partition. [2] | `cp`; `ifl`; `icf` |

**[1] `virtualization.partition.id`:** A platform-specific opaque identifier that uniquely identifies this partition within its virtualization platform. On IBM Z in PR/SM (classic) mode this is the partition object-id assigned by the HMC.

**[2] `virtualization.partition.cpu.type`:** Identifies the processor type being counted. Use `all` for the total count across all processor types.

---

`virtualization.partition.cpu.type` has the following list of well-known values. If one of them applies, then the respective value MUST be used; otherwise, a custom value MAY be used.

| Value | Description | Stability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `aap` | Application Assist Processor (zAAP) — a specialty IBM Z processor for Java workloads, deprecated in z13 and later models. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `all` | Aggregate across all processor types allocated to this partition. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `cbp` | Coupling Bus Processor (CBP) — a processor type dedicated to HiperSockets network coupling on IBM Z. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `cp` | Central Processor (CP) — the general-purpose IBM Z processor type. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `icf` | Internal Coupling Facility (ICF) — a processor type used for sysplex coupling on IBM Z. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `ifl` | Integrated Facility for Linux (IFL) — a processor type optimised for Linux workloads on IBM Z. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `iip` | z Integrated Information Processor (zIIP) — a specialty engine for eligible Java and DB2 workloads on IBM Z. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `unknown` | Processor type is not known or the platform does not differentiate by processor type. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |

## `virtualization.partition.cpu.utilization`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `virtualization.partition.cpu.utilization` | Gauge | `1` | The fraction of time processors allocated to the firmware partition were busy executing work, as a ratio from 0 (idle) to 1 (fully utilised). [2] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.partition` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[2]:** Reports CPU utilization for a hardware or firmware enforced partition such as an IBM Z logical partition (LPAR) managed by PR/SM (Processor Resource/Systems Manager). Unlike `virtualization.vm.cpu.utilization`, this metric applies to partitions managed at the firmware level rather than by a software hypervisor. In IBM Z PR/SM (classic mode) this maps to the processor-usage fields in the logical-partition-usage metric group from the HMC Web Services API. The `virtualization.partition.cpu.type` attribute breaks down utilization by processor specialisation type (cp, ifl, icf, iip, etc.). Analogous to `mainframe.partition.cpu.utilization` in the mainframe namespace.

[3] | `0abc1234-5678-90ab-cdef-1234567890ab`; `partition-3` |
| [`virtualization.partition.cpu.type`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-partition-cpu-type) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The category of processor type allocated to the firmware partition. [4] | `cp`; `ifl`; `icf` |

**[3] `virtualization.partition.id`:** A platform-specific opaque identifier that uniquely identifies this partition within its virtualization platform. On IBM Z in PR/SM (classic) mode this is the partition object-id assigned by the HMC.

**[4] `virtualization.partition.cpu.type`:** Identifies the processor type whose utilization is being reported. Use `all` for an aggregate across all types. Omit on platforms that do not differentiate by processor type.

## `virtualization.partition.state.code`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `virtualization.partition.state.code` | Gauge | `1` | The operational state of the firmware partition encoded as a numeric gauge (1=in this state, 0=not in this state). [4] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.partition` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[4]:** Reports the current lifecycle state of the partition. For each partition, exactly one state value will be 1 at any given time; all others will be 0. This encoding enables Prometheus alerting rules and state-change detection without label-value cardinality issues. In IBM Z PR/SM (classic mode) this maps to the status field reported by the HMC Web Services API for the logical partition object. Valid state values are defined by the `virtualization.partition.state` attribute enum (active, not_activated, stopped, unknown). Analogous to `mainframe.partition.status.code` in the mainframe namespace.

**Attributes:**

| Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`virtualization.partition.id`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-partition-id) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | Unique identifier for the hardware or firmware partition. [6] | `0abc1234-5678-90ab-cdef-1234567890ab`; `partition-3` |
| [`virtualization.partition.state`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-partition-state) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | The operational state of the partition. [7] | `active`; `not_activated`; `stopped` |

**[6] `virtualization.partition.id`:** A platform-specific opaque identifier that uniquely identifies this partition within its virtualization platform. On IBM Z in PR/SM (classic) mode this is the partition object-id assigned by the HMC.

**[7] `virtualization.partition.state`:** The state whose membership is being reported. One record per state value is emitted per partition; the value is 1 for the current state and 0 for all others.

---

`virtualization.partition.state` has the following list of well-known values. If one of them applies, then the respective value MUST be used; otherwise, a custom value MAY be used.

| Value | Description | Stability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `active` | Partition is active and processing workloads. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `not_activated` | Partition is defined but not yet activated. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `stopped` | Partition has been deactivated. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `unknown` | Partition state is not known. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |

## `virtualization.platform.cpu.utilization`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `virtualization.platform.cpu.utilization` | Gauge | `1` | The fraction of total physical CPU capacity of the virtualization platform currently in use across all hosted workloads and hypervisor overhead, as a ratio from 0 (idle) to 1 (fully utilised). [5] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.platform` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[5]:** Reports aggregate CPU utilization at the physical platform level, combining processor time consumed by all hosted partitions or virtual machines plus hypervisor overhead. In IBM Z PR/SM (classic mode) this maps to the processor-usage-* fields in the cpc-usage-overview metric group from the HMC Web Services API. In IBM z/VM it corresponds to CP pool utilization. In VMware ESXi it corresponds to the host-level cpu.usage.average performance counter. In Microsoft Hyper-V it corresponds to the "% Total Run Time" counter on the Hyper-V Hypervisor Logical Processor object, aggregated across all physical processors. Analogous to `mainframe.host.cpu.utilization` in the mainframe namespace.

**Attributes:**

| Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`host.name`](/docs/registry/host/README.md#host-name) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | Name of the host. On Unix systems, it may contain what the hostname command returns, or the fully qualified hostname, or another name specified by the user. [8] | `opentelemetry-test` |

**[8] `host.name`:** The name of the virtualization platform (host) this measurement belongs to. This is the identity attribute of the virtualization.platform entity. HMC source: CPC object field `name`.

## `virtualization.platform.memory.total`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `virtualization.platform.memory.total` | Gauge | `MiBy` | The total physical memory installed in the virtualization platform, in mebibytes (MiB). [6] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.platform` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[6]:** Reports the total physical RAM available to the hypervisor before any allocations. In IBM Z PR/SM (classic mode) this maps to the storage-total-installed-memory field on the CPC (Central Processing Complex) object in the HMC Web Services API. In VMware ESXi it corresponds to mem.total.average converted from kilobytes to mebibytes. In Microsoft Hyper-V it corresponds to the total physical memory property of the host system. In IBM z/VM it corresponds to the total real storage of the underlying system. This value is typically static for the lifetime of the platform. Analogous to `mainframe.host.memory.size` (type=total) in the mainframe namespace.

On Unix systems, it may contain what the hostname command returns, or the fully qualified hostname, or another name specified by the user. [9] | `opentelemetry-test` |

**[9] `host.name`:** The name of the virtualization platform (host) this measurement belongs to. HMC source: CPC object field `name`.

## `virtualization.platform.memory.used`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `virtualization.platform.memory.used` | Gauge | `MiBy` | The amount of physical memory on the virtualization platform currently allocated to hosted workloads and hypervisor overhead, in mebibytes (MiB). [7] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.platform` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[7]:** Reports the physical memory in active use as seen by the hypervisor. The difference between `virtualization.platform.memory.total` and this metric gives the available free memory. In IBM Z PR/SM (classic mode) this is derived from storage-total-installed-memory minus storage-available-memory on the CPC object in the HMC Web Services API. In VMware ESXi it corresponds to mem.usage.average converted from kilobytes to mebibytes. In Microsoft Hyper-V it corresponds to (total physical memory) minus (available memory) as reported by the host operating system performance counters.

| `virtualization.platform.partition.count` | UpDownCounter | `{partition}` | The number of firmware-enforced partitions currently active on the virtualization platform. [8] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.platform` |

**[11] `host.name`:** The name of the virtualization platform (host) this count belongs to. HMC source: CPC object field `name`.

## `virtualization.platform.power.usage`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `virtualization.platform.power.usage` | Gauge | `W` | The total power consumption of the virtualization platform hardware in Watts. [9] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.platform` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[9]:** Reports the aggregate power draw of the physical platform including all processors, memory, I/O adapters, and cooling infrastructure. In IBM Z PR/SM (classic mode) and DPM mode this maps to the `power` field in the zcpc-environmentals-and-power metric group from the HMC Web Services API; the HMC reports the value in kilowatts (kW) which must be converted to Watts by multiplying by 1000. In VMware ESXi it corresponds to the power.power performance counter on the host object which is already in Watts. In Microsoft Hyper-V it corresponds to platform power data available from IPMI or vendor management agents. Analogous to `mainframe.host.power.usage` in the mainframe namespace.

**[10]:** Reports the count of virtual machines (VMs) currently known to the hypervisor. The optional `virtualization.platform.vm.state` attribute enables breakdown by running, stopped, paused, or all. In IBM z/VM this corresponds to the number of active guest virtual machines. In VMware ESXi it corresponds to numVms on the host summary object. In Microsoft Hyper-V it corresponds to the number of virtual machine objects known to the hypervisor. Not applicable on IBM Z PR/SM (classic mode) which uses firmware partitions rather than software VMs — use `virtualization.platform.partition.count` on that platform.

On Unix systems, it may contain what the hostname command returns, or the fully qualified hostname, or another name specified by the user. [14] | `opentelemetry-test` |

[15] | `running`; `stopped`; `paused` |

**[14] `host.name`:** The name of the virtualization platform (host) this count belongs to. HMC source: CPC object field `name`.

**[15] `virtualization.platform.vm.state`:** When present, the count is filtered to VMs in the specified power state. When absent or set to `all`, the count covers all VMs regardless of state.

## `virtualization.vm.cpu.ready_time`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `virtualization.vm.cpu.ready_time` | Gauge | `1` | The fraction of time the virtual machine's virtual CPUs (vCPUs) were ready to run but waiting for physical CPU time from the hypervisor, as a ratio from 0 to 1. [12] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.vm` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[12]:** Measures hypervisor scheduling contention from the guest's perspective. High ready time indicates the physical host is overcommitted and vCPUs are competing for physical CPU time. In IBM z/VM this corresponds to the dispatch wait time per guest. In VMware ESXi it corresponds to the cpu.ready.summation counter converted from milliseconds to a ratio by dividing by (measurement_interval_ms). In Microsoft Hyper-V it corresponds to "% Hypervisor Run Time" on the Hyper-V Virtual Processor object. Not directly available in IBM Z PR/SM (classic mode) — implementations may omit this metric on that platform.

## `virtualization.vm.cpu.steal_time`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `virtualization.vm.cpu.steal_time` | Gauge | `1` | The fraction of time the virtual machine's virtual CPUs (vCPUs) were runnable but could not execute because the hypervisor was running other guests, as a ratio from 0 to 1. [13] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.vm` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[13]:** CPU steal time quantifies the scheduling overhead imposed by the hypervisor on this VM. A high steal time indicates the physical host is overcommitted and the hypervisor is not honouring the VM's CPU allocations. This is distinct from `virtualization.vm.cpu.ready_time` which measures time waiting in the scheduler queue. In KVM (libvirt) environments it corresponds to the steal_time field from virDomainGetCPUStats(), converted to a ratio by dividing by (elapsed_ns × vCPU_count). In OpenShift Virtualization (KubeVirt) it corresponds to the kubevirt_vmi_vcpu_wait_seconds_total counter rate-converted to a ratio. Not available on IBM Z PR/SM (classic mode), IBM z/VM, VMware ESXi, or Microsoft Hyper-V — implementations on those platforms should omit this metric.

[19] | `worker-node-01`; `compute-az1-007`; `rhcos-node-03` |

**[18] `virtualization.vm.id`:** A UUID or other platform-specific opaque identifier that uniquely identifies this virtual machine within the hypervisor. Analogous to `host.id` for physical machines or a container ID for containers.

**[19] `virtualization.vm.node.name`:** The Kubernetes node (or KVM host) on which the VM is running. High steal time on one node may indicate host overcommitment specific to that node's physical CPU count.

## `virtualization.vm.cpu.utilization`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `virtualization.vm.cpu.utilization` | Gauge | `1` | The fraction of time the virtual machine's virtual CPUs (vCPUs) were busy executing work, as a ratio from 0 (idle) to 1 (fully utilised). [14] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.vm` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[14]:** Measures active execution time from the guest's perspective, aggregated across all vCPUs. In IBM Z PR/SM (classic mode) this maps to the processor-usage fields in the logical-partition-usage metric group via the HMC Web Services API. In IBM z/VM it corresponds to CP usage per guest virtual machine. In VMware ESXi it corresponds to the cpu.usage.average performance counter. In Microsoft Hyper-V it corresponds to the "% Total Run Time" counter on the Hyper-V Virtual Processor object. In KVM (libvirt) environments it corresponds to the cpu_time field from the virDomainGetCPUStats() API, converted to a ratio by dividing by (elapsed_ns × vCPU_count). In OpenShift Virtualization (KubeVirt) it corresponds to the kubevirt_vmi_cpu_usage_seconds_total counter, rate-converted to a ratio. A value of 1 means all vCPUs were 100% busy during the measurement interval.

## `virtualization.vm.memory.balloon`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `virtualization.vm.memory.balloon` | Gauge | `MiBy` | The amount of memory reclaimed from the virtual machine by the hypervisor's memory ballooning mechanism, in mebibytes (MiB). [18] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.vm` |

**[18]:** Memory ballooning is a technique where the hypervisor inflates a balloon driver inside the guest OS to reclaim memory under host pressure. A non-zero value indicates the hypervisor is reclaiming memory from this VM. In VMware ESXi this corresponds to mem.vmmemctl.average converted from kilobytes to mebibytes. In Microsoft Hyper-V it relates to memory pressure adjustments via the Dynamic Memory mechanism. Not applicable on IBM Z PR/SM or IBM z/VM — implementations on those platforms should omit this metric or report 0.

## `virtualization.vm.memory.rss`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `virtualization.vm.memory.rss` | Gauge | `MiBy` | The amount of physical host memory (resident set size) currently mapped to the virtual machine's address space, in mebibytes (MiB). [19] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.vm` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[19]:** Resident Set Size (RSS) reports the actual physical host memory pages that back the VM at a given moment. Unlike `virtualization.vm.memory.allocated` (which reflects the configured allocation), RSS reflects real consumption accounting for memory ballooning, KSM (Kernel Same-page Merging), and huge page backing. A VM with high allocated memory but low RSS is not causing physical memory pressure. In KVM (libvirt) environments it corresponds to the rss field from the memory.stat output of virDomainMemoryStats(), converted from kilobytes to mebibytes. In OpenShift Virtualization (KubeVirt) it corresponds to the kubevirt_vmi_memory_resident_bytes metric (converted from bytes to MiB). Not directly available on IBM Z PR/SM, IBM z/VM, VMware ESXi, or Microsoft Hyper-V — implementations on those platforms should omit this metric or approximate it using `virtualization.vm.memory.used`.

[28] | `worker-node-01`; `compute-az1-007`; `rhcos-node-03` |

In Microsoft Hyper-V it corresponds to the "Bytes Received/sec" and "Bytes Sent/sec" counters on the Hyper-V Virtual Network Adapter object, accumulated as a counter.

| Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |

| [`network.io.direction`](/docs/registry/network/README.md#network-io-direction) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | The network IO operation direction. [31] | `receive`; `transmit` |
| [`virtualization.vm.id`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-vm-id) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | Unique identifier for the virtual machine instance. [32] | `vm-0abc1234`; `8c3f2a1b-4d56-4e78-9f01-2a3b4c5d6e7f` |
| [`virtualization.vm.network.interface.name`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-vm-network-interface-name) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The name of the virtual network interface (vNIC) attached to the virtual machine. [33] | `Network adapter 1`; `eth0`; `vmxnet3-0` |

**[31] `network.io.direction`:** One of `receive` or `transmit`. Upstream OTel attribute used to disambiguate receive vs. transmit byte counts on the same interface.

**[32] `virtualization.vm.id`:** A UUID or other platform-specific opaque identifier that uniquely identifies this virtual machine within the hypervisor. Analogous to `host.id` for physical machines or a container ID for containers.

**[33] `virtualization.vm.network.interface.name`:** The virtual NIC name as reported by the hypervisor. Omit when reporting aggregated across all interfaces on the VM.

`network.io.direction` has the following list of well-known values. If one of them applies, then the respective value MUST be used; otherwise, a custom value MAY be used.

| Value | Description | Stability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `receive` | receive | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `transmit` | transmit | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |

## `virtualization.vm.power.state`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `virtualization.vm.power.state` | Gauge | `1` | The current power state of the virtual machine encoded as a numeric gauge (1=in this state, 0=not in this state). [23] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.vm` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[23]:** Reports the operational lifecycle state of the VM as a dimensioned gauge. For each VM, exactly one state value will be 1 at any given time; all others will be 0. This encoding enables Prometheus alerting rules and state-change detection without label-value cardinality issues. In IBM Z PR/SM (classic mode) this maps to the partition status field on the logical-partition object via the HMC Web Services API. In IBM z/VM it maps to guest state. In VMware ESXi it maps to runtime.powerState. In Microsoft Hyper-V it maps to the VM operational state property.

**Attributes:**

| Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`virtualization.vm.id`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-vm-id) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | Unique identifier for the virtual machine instance. [34] | `vm-0abc1234`; `8c3f2a1b-4d56-4e78-9f01-2a3b4c5d6e7f` |
| [`virtualization.vm.state`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-vm-state) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | The operational state of the virtual machine. [35] | `running`; `stopped`; `paused` |

**[34] `virtualization.vm.id`:** A UUID or other platform-specific opaque identifier that uniquely identifies this virtual machine within the hypervisor. Analogous to `host.id` for physical machines or a container ID for containers.

**[35] `virtualization.vm.state`:** The state whose membership is being reported. One record per state value is emitted per VM; the value is 1 for the current state and 0 for all others.

---

`virtualization.vm.state` has the following list of well-known values. If one of them applies, then the respective value MUST be used; otherwise, a custom value MAY be used.

| Value | Description | Stability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `failed` | Virtual machine has encountered a fatal error and cannot recover without operator intervention. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `migrating` | Virtual machine is being live-migrated to another host without interruption. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `paused` | Virtual machine is suspended with state preserved in memory. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `running` | Virtual machine is running and processing workloads. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `scheduled` | Virtual machine has been assigned to a host node and is being prepared to start. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `scheduling` | Virtual machine has been requested but is waiting for the scheduler to assign it to a host node. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `stopped` | Virtual machine is stopped and not consuming CPU resources. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `succeeded` | Virtual machine completed its workload and terminated cleanly (applicable to batch or ephemeral VMs). | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `unknown` | Virtual machine state is not known or cannot be determined. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
